checks.name: Public updater feed selects the expected new release
Previous executable matches the published v3.2.3 checksum
Published new executable matches its manifest checksum
Previous executable starts through the desktop shortcut
Previous application automatically detects the newly published release
No automatic download occurs before Download is clicked
Download through the application completes and stages verified release bytes
Previous native application browser session is observed before installation
All browser processes for the old application profile close during the real upgrade
No unexpected dialog is silently accepted during the upgrade
Actual new native browser uses guest mode with extensions and sync disabled
Native helper installs and restarts the new version
New application confirms a rendered interface and a visible owned native window
User settings remain byte-identical after the real upgrade
Exactly the previous published executable is retained for rollback
Only one rollback executable generation is retained
Desktop shortcut target remains the same stable executable path
Installed target bytes match the new public release across staging volumes
Manual update check succeeds on the new executable
Short manual-check cooldown prevents another request
Application focus binding checks again after two minutes
Native automatic checks continue after five active minutes
Owned download staging is cleaned after the update
Existing desktop shortcut launches the updated executable
Missing healthy-start confirmation triggers the actual native rollback path
Rollback restores the previous executable bytes at a legacy versioned filename
Rollback relaunches the previous application
Rollback preserves user settings
Fixed application produces no unexpected modal dialogs throughout the test

limitations: UAC consent transitions were not exercised.
Playwright drives the application page alongside its visible native Edge window; physical desktop interaction was not performed.
Offline, HTTP failure, rate limiting, ETag and malicious-file cases use deterministic native Go tests.
Legacy Windows Server versions and every server-role collector were not exercised.

checks.name: Published v3.2.3 negative control reproduces the status-0 popup after shutdown
Fixed page stops polling, aborts in-flight XHRs, and ignores focus/visibility after install acceptance
Failed manual update action is shown inline with zero modal alerts
Rejected installation restores the controls and active state polling without modal errors

limits: The user Microsoft account, synced extensions and organization policies were not reproduced.
Hosted Windows Server 2025 and Edge were tested. Human desktop and UAC consent were not tested.
Playwright drives the real application page alongside its visible native Edge window. Focus uses a synthetic DOM event after a real wait.
Offline, HTTP, rate-limit, cache and malicious-file cases use deterministic native Go tests.
Live inventory/report workflows, Chrome guest fallback and legacy Windows versions were not tested.
SHA-256 validates bytes against the HTTPS manifest, not publisher signing.
Prior releases/tags/assets were preserved. Repository-level immutable release locking is disabled; workflow overwrite guards remain.
